summary: The article provides a largely accurate overview of Maruti Suzuki's Q1 FY27 performance, with most key financial figures and strategic initiatives aligning with authoritative reports.

claims.claim: Operating revenue surged 36% year-on-year to ₹52,456 crore, with sales volumes up 29% to 683,000 units.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm operating revenue of ₹52,456 crore (or very close, e.g., ₹52,469.8 crore) and sales volumes of 683,000 units (or 682,724 units), both up around 36% and 29% respectively.

claims.claim: net profit declined by 9-11% due to rising raw material costs and a strategic decision to shorten vendor settlement terms.
claims.note: Net profit declined by 9.1% (consolidated) or 10.8-11% (standalone) due to rising raw material costs and the strategic decision to shorten vendor settlement terms.

claims.claim: EBITDA margin contracted significantly to 8.2% from 12% in the previous year, primarily due to increased material costs.
claims.note: EBITDA margin contracted to 8.2% (or 8.6% in some standalone reports) from 12% (or 12.6%) in the previous year, primarily due to increased material costs.

claims.claim: Material costs as a percentage of net sales surged to 80.5% in Q1 FY27, up from 74.5% in Q1 FY26, representing a significant adverse movement of 600 basis points.
claims.note: Material costs as a percentage of net sales increased to 80.5% in Q1 FY27 from 74.5% in Q1 FY26, a rise of 600 basis points.

claims.claim: The commissioning of its second manufacturing plant at Kharkhoda and the start of a fourth line at Hansalpur in Gujarat have added approximately 500,000 units of annual capacity, bringing the total to roughly 2.9 million units.
claims.note: The second plant at Kharkhoda (250,000 units) and the fourth line at Hansalpur (250,000 units) have added 500,000 units of annual capacity, bringing the total to 2.9 million units.

claims.claim: The board also approved an initial investment of ₹561 crore for four compressed biogas (CBG) manufacturing projects, signalling a push towards alternative fuel vehicles.
claims.note: The board approved an initial investment of ₹561 crore for four compressed biogas (CBG) manufacturing projects.

claims.claim: The company also launched India's first flex-fuel car during the quarter.
claims.note: Maruti Suzuki launched India's first flex-fuel car (WagonR) in June 2026, which falls within Q1 FY27.

article_title: Maruti Suzuki's Q1 FY27: Navigating Headwinds Towards Growth
